blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Representation-alignment methods effectively accelerate the diffusion transformer training. REPA, for example, uses a pretrained vision encoder to supervise an intermediate layer through an MLP projection head which is discarded after training. It aims to import semantics from the vision encoder to the diffusion backbone. While this objective is achieved at early layers by back-propagating the alignment loss, there is no guarantee that later layers, supervised by the velocity prediction loss alone, can well access such semantics. We propose a simple solution, representation conditioning (RECON), to improve semantics in later layers. During training, we feed the pretrained vision encoder tokens into later layers; during inference, because we no longer have the clean image, we reuse the MLP head (as a proxy to the vision encoder) and project its output tokens to the later layers. Our method adds no parameters and leads to much faster convergence: RECON is $63\times$ faster than SiT and $25\times$ faster than REPA. Code is available at https://github.com/saeidrazavi/RECON

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
An effective strategy for efficient diffusion transformer training is to align the diffusion features with an external vision encoder ( Yu et al., 2025 ) .
Specifically, REPA ( Yu et al., 2025 ) uses a lightweight projection head g ϕ g_{\phi} 1 1 1 We use g ϕ g_{\phi} interchangeably with “projection head”. Project page: recondiffusion.github.io to map the intermediate features of diffusion backbone to be similar to those of the frozen vision encoder (Fig. 1 a ).
Several follow-up works build on this idea, e.g. , REG ( Wu et al., 2025 ) ,
DDT ( Wang et al., 2026 ) and REPA-E ( Leng et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en: By aligning the diffusion model with an external vision encoder, the assumption is that the diffusion backbone will effectively access and use the semantic features, so that generation will eventually improve. In this work, we examine the alignment between the vision encoder features and features of each layer of the diffusion transformer, and the feature from g ϕ g_{\phi} . We find that the feature from g ϕ g_{\phi} has the highest level of alignment with the vision encoder, as shown in Fig. 2 b . This finding is not surprising, because g ϕ g_{\phi} is physically closest to the vision encoder and is directly optimized to minimize alignment loss.

blocks.en: Surprisingly, despite its strong alignment with the vision encoder, existing methods typically discard the projection head g ϕ g_{\phi} after training, as shown in Fig. 1 a . We argue that the practice is a waste of model resources including learned weights and semantics: the full potential of representation alignment is not achieved.

blocks.en:
We introduce a very simple fix, named REpresentation CONditioning (RECON). Our idea is that instead of removing g ϕ g_{\phi} after training, we keep it and use it as a proxy of the vision encoder during inference, so that strong semantics from g ϕ g_{\phi} can be explicitly used to benefit generation. Specifically, during inference, RECON pools the g ϕ g_{\phi} output features into semantic tokens , concatenates
them with the patch tokens, and lets the diffusion backbone attend to both types of tokens. Correspondingly, we have a small modification for training recipe: during training, the semantic tokens directly come from the vision encoder and serve as condition for the backbone.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Representation alignment. REPA ( Yu et al., 2025 ) is a representative work.
DDT ( Wang et al., 2026 ) builds the separation into the architecture,
dividing the transformer into a semantic encoder and a velocity decoder and
applying the alignment loss to the encoder output.
VA-VAE ( Yao et al., 2025 ) moves the alignment out of the generator into the latent
space.
REPA-E ( Leng et al., 2025 ) makes joint optimization of VAE and diffusion backbone possible. What is common in all these works is discarding the projection head after training, which, as we argue, is not optimal.
Another line of works relies on the supervisory signal from the model itself rather than external vision encoder. SRA ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) distills the
representation of a later layer at low noise into an earlier layer at high
noise. Self-Flow ( Chefer et al., 2026 ) instead creates information asymmetry
across tokens by assigning them different noise levels, so the model has to
infer corrupted tokens from cleaner ones. We provide a more detailed related-work discussion in Appendix A .

blocks.en: We are motivated by the following three considerations.
blocks.zh: 我们受到以下三个考虑的激励。

blocks.en: First , stronger alignment with external vision encoder positively correlates with better generation. For different REPA checkpoints, we plot their CKNNA and generation FID (gFID) in Fig. 2 a . CKNNA compares the nearest-neighbor structure of two representations; a higher CKNNA score means higher alignment. The figure demonstrates that alignment and generation improve together.

blocks.en: 5 Proposed Representation Conditioning (RECON)

blocks.en: Overview. The key is to retain g ϕ ​ ( h ) g_{\phi}(h) . At inference, we fuse the output of g ϕ ​ ( h ) g_{\phi}(h) with the diffusion patch tokens, which serves as in-context conditioning for the later diffusion layers. Before fusion, the g ϕ ​ ( h ) g_{\phi}(h) output is pooled into a few semantic tokens . During training, we directly use the vision encoder features and pool them into semantic tokens, called teacher forcing , because the projection layer is being trained and thus not stable. Using perception model features for training and projected features for inference creates a distribution gap. We mitigate this through a time-dependent scheduling for semantic token injection . Overall framework is depicted in Fig. 1 b and 1 c . We detail these components below.

blocks.en: 7 Discussions
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en: Why do later layers need more semantics? Later layers are only supervised by the flow-matching loss and only depend on h h . In comparison, the gradient of REPA loss is back-propagated to early layers, so early layers are optimized towards higher semantics. By injecting semantics to late layers, the late layers, through training, can decide whether to use them or not, which is at least not detrimental and turns out to be beneficial.
blocks.zh: 为什么后层需要更多的语义学? 后来的地层仅由流量相匹配的损耗所监督,而只取决于h h. 相较之下,REPA损失的梯度被反向地层传播到早期地层,因此早期地层被优化到更高的语义上. 通过将语义学注入后层,后层通过训练可以决定是否使用,这至少不会有害,结果也是有益的.

blocks.en: Rethinking guidance for semantically rich diffusion models. CFG helps RECON less than it helps standard diffusion transformers. Our hunch is that with the semantic tokens, the backbone is already rich in semantics without the class label, so the unconditional prediction is close to the conditional one. RAE ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) reports a similar observation, and like RAE, we use Autoguidance ( Karras et al., 2024 ) . We further improve Autoguidance with two simple changes at sampling time, Projected Autoguidance (Appendix C.1 ) and Semantic Token Extrapolation (Appendix C.2 ). They improve gFID from 2.26 → 2.09 2.26\to 2.09 at 80 epochs and from 1.80 → 1.49 1.80\to 1.49 at 480 epochs. We see these as first steps. One promising direction is Internal Guidance ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) , which uses an intermediate layer of the model as the weak model. Another is guidance that acts directly on the semantic tokens, rather than on the velocity.

RAE(Zheng等,2026年)报告类似观察,与RAE一样,我们使用"自动指导"(Karras等,2024年). 我们进一步改进了自动指导,在取样时进行了两个简单的改变,即预测自动指导(附录C.1)和语义Token外推(附录C.2)。 它们从80个纪元的 2.26 ~ 2.09 2.26\ 2.09到480个纪元的 1.80 ~ 1.49 1.80\ 1.49到1.49 。 我们认为这些是第一步。 一个很有希望的方向是"内部指导"(周等,2026年),它使用模型的中间层作为弱模型. 另一个是直接作用于语义符号而不是速度的指针.

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en: This paper challenges the practice in representation alignment methods that the projection head g ϕ g_{\phi} should be discarded after training. This is based on our observation that the output of g ϕ g_{\phi} is very semantical: it aligns with the vision encoder more strongly than any of the diffusion transformer layers. Discarding it means we forfeit useful and also free cues. We propose representation conditioning (RECON), which supplies output of g ϕ g_{\phi} to the later layers. With no added parameters and no change in training loss, RECON simply lets later layers decide how to use the conditioning semantics. We report good improvement over REPA in various settings. We hope that RECON was effective in conveying and bringing up the following message: what matters in representation alignment is not only acquiring a representation, but also keeping it accessible in generation.

Additionally, we used Claude Code to draft the paper outline, check the grammar of the manuscript, and improve the clarity of the writing. We also used it to generate most of the figures and tables from our experiment logs and checkpoints, following the colour palette we provided. We have reviewed all AI-assisted work, including the code, experiment configurations, figures, tables, and text. We take responsibility for the final content of this work and the associated codebase, including all materials produced with AI assistance.

blocks.en:
Diffusion transformers. DiT ( Peebles & Xie, 2023 ) replaced the
U-Net of latent diffusion ( Rombach et al., 2022 ) with a transformer and
showed that generation quality improves with model compute. SiT ( Ma et al., 2024 ) keeps the DiT architecture and trains it with the
interpolant framework, which is the setting we follow. Other works change
the architecture or add objectives during training: U-ViT ( Bao et al., 2023 ) adds long skip connections between shallow and deep
blocks, DiffiT ( Hatamizadeh et al., 2024 ) makes self-attention
time-dependent, and MDT ( Gao et al., 2023 ) , MaskDiT ( Zheng et al., 2024 ) and SD-DiT ( Zhu et al., 2024 ) add masking or self-supervised objectives.
For text-to-image generation, MMDiT ( Esser et al., 2024 ) keeps text and
image tokens in separate streams that interact through joint attention.

Pretrained representations in the latent space. Instead of
aligning the generator, some works build the semantics into the latent
space itself. VA-VAE and REPA-E (Section 2 ) align or
fine-tune the VAE. RAE ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) goes further and replaces the
VAE encoder with a frozen pretrained representation encoder such as DINOv2,
training only a decoder and running diffusion in that representation space.
These approaches are complementary to RECON: in our tokenizer experiments
(Fig. 8(b) ), RECON still improves generation on VA-VAE,
although by a smaller margin than on SD-VAE.

blocks.en:
Train–inference gaps and forcing strategies. Conditioning a model
on information during training that is not available at inference is a
well-known problem. In autoregressive video diffusion, teacher forcing conditions on context
that the model must later produce itself, and Self Forcing ( Huang et al., 2025 ) closes the resulting gap by rolling out the
model during training. RECON has the same kind of gap: it uses teacher
forcing, conditioning on vision encoder features during training and on the
output of g ϕ g_{\phi} at inference. We reduce this gap with time-dependent
scheduling for semantic token injection (Section 5 ).

Computing resources. All models are trained on 4 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.
In our default setting (SiT-XL/2, batch size 256), training runs at about
4.10 iterations per second. A 400K-iteration run (80 epochs) therefore takes
about 27 hours (about 110 GPU-hours), and the longest 2.4M-iteration run
(480 epochs) about 6.8 days (about 650 GPU-hours). RECON adds only k = 1 k=1 semantic token to the 256 patch tokens of the later layers, so its training
cost is almost the same as that of REPA.

blocks.en:
Relation to APG. The projection comes from APG ( Sadat et al., 2025 ) , which splits the CFG update into parts parallel and
orthogonal to the conditional prediction. We differ from APG in three ways.
First, we apply the projection to Autoguidance instead of CFG. Second, we
project at each spatial position, while APG projects the whole latent at
once; per-position projection gave a lower FID in our experiments. Third, we
only drop the parallel part. APG also keeps a down-weighted parallel part
and adds rescaling and momentum, which we do not use.
blocks.zh:
与APG的关系. 预测来自APG(Sadat等人,2025年),它将CFG更新分为平行部分和
与条件预测垂直。 我们与APG在三个方面不同.
首先,我们把投影应用于自动指导而不是CFG. 第二,我们
在每一个空间位置上进行项目,而APG则在

forcing, Section 5.1 ). During sampling, it is predicted by

sample. At high noise levels, it is hard to tell what the final image will
look like, so the predicted token is close to the average token of the
class and is less specific to the sample. As a result, at high noise
levels the predicted semantic token is more typical of its class than the token of
the final generated image.

blocks.en:
We follow the linear probing protocol of MAE ( He et al., 2022 ) . For each layer, we take the frozen features of the
400K-iteration EMA checkpoint at t = 0.25 t=0.25 . We use the null class
label, so that no label information leaks into the features. As for CKNNA,

affine parameters, followed by a linear layer. We train it on the ImageNet-1K

recipe, which trains for 90 epochs, we train the classifier for 20 epochs to
reduce the cost of probing every layer. REPA and RECON use the same schedule,
so the comparison between them is fair.

Is the gain bottlenecked by the tokenizer? RECON improves
generation on all three tokenizers, but by different amounts
(Table 11 ). FID goes from 7.84 → 3.25 7.84\to 3.25 on SD-VAE and 7.41 → 4.78 7.41\to 4.78 on InVAE, but only from 4.95 → 4.02 4.95\to 4.02 on VA-VAE. VA-VAE is

latent that is already semantically organized, and a signal with information
that the latent does not contain could still help. Telling these two apart
would show whether RECON is close to its limit on such tokenizers, or whether
a different way of injecting semantics could give further gains.

the way. RECON commits to the subject within the first few steps and then
refines it, while the estimates of REPA stay blurry for much longer. As a
